evidence.text_span: Latent infection process representing the number of people infected over time; used as the modelled infections in the renewal equation and as the source of deaths through the infection-to-death distribution.
Observed and modelled COVID-19-related deaths used to fit the model.
Effective reproduction number; modeled as a function of the initial reproduction number and intervention effects.
evidence.value: time-varying; piecewise constant with changes at interventions

evidence.text_span: Initial reproduction number before interventions took effect.
Fraction of infections resulting in death.
evidence.value: population-averaged; adjusted for age structure and contact patterns

evidence.text_span: Delay distribution linking infections to observed deaths.
evidence.value: derived from onset-to-symptoms and symptoms-to-death distributions

evidence.text_span: Distribution weighting the discrete convolution of previous infections in the renewal equation.
evidence.value: approximated using the serial interval distribution

evidence.text_span: Distribution of time between symptom onset in a primary case and a secondary case.
evidence.value: used as approximation to generation time distribution

evidence.text_span: Covariate effects of governmental interventions on transmission, including lockdown, public events banned, school closure, self isolation, and social distancing encouraged.
evidence.value: country-shared with partial pooling for the last intervention
